units.function: Large embedded-Postgres service suite for reusable routine CRUD/revisions, Secret bindings, triggers/webhooks, variable resolution, responsible-human snapshots, issue/heartbeat dispatch, concurrency coalescing, workspaces, scheduling/catch-up/activity gates, Agent validity and failure cleanup.
units.dependencyDirection: Routine service is the orchestration owner over routine/document revisions, trigger and Secret services, projects/workspaces, issue creation/inbox, heartbeat wakeup, activity log and scheduler; provider registry and runtime environment are injectable seams.
units.keyDataModels: Routine/template revision snapshot and dispatch fingerprint; responsibleUserId; variable definitions/resolved values; env plain/secret_ref and Company bindings; schedule/webhook trigger, public ID/signing mode/replay window; routine run statuses/reasons; issue origin/fingerprint/workspace; heartbeat liveness; activity gate; Agent reporting chain; worktree activation cutoff.
units.lifecycle: Create/version/restore a template; validate assignment and Secret references; configure/rotate/delete schedules or webhooks; resolve inputs/workspaces/effective responsible human; serialize dispatch; create execution issue and queue Agent; coalesce/skip/fail/clean up; tick/catch up schedules and evaluate activity/project/worktree gates.
units.testAssessment: The 57 source-level cases are one of Paperclip's strongest service suites and cover many incident-derived edge cases: append-only restore, stale conflicts, safe trigger snapshots, responsibility drift, terminated reporting chains, concurrent dispatch, queue cleanup, pause/cutoff and schedule replay. They were skipped locally because embedded PostgreSQL is unavailable. The suite remains initiation-centric and omits authoritative terminal results/evidence, approval/data/model/tool/budget snapshots, service-call authorization and hardened public-webhook abuse/replay cases.
units.designRationale: Use a versioned reusable-work aggregate that instantiates ordinary issues and heartbeat execution, preserving compatibility with existing task/inbox/workspace systems while containing duplicate, stale, unsafe-assignee and missed-schedule behavior.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral repeatable work and schedules that a human can safely delegate to Agents, with exact responsibility/authorization snapshots, deterministic recovery and no credential/data leakage across managed and self-hosted execution planes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT as a strong reference candidate for reusable-work orchestration: append-only revisions/restores, base-revision conflicts, dispatch fingerprints, effective responsible-user snapshot, Agent/reporting-chain validation, Secret binding indexes with value-free snapshots, concurrent coalescing, wakeup completion/failure cleanup, project pause and bounded catch-up concepts. Add explicit execution-intent idempotency, cross-node tests, typed sensitive inputs, immutable Agent/model/tool/Secret/Data/Budget/Risk contract digest, approval pause/resume and terminal evidence/result states. Require authenticated signed webhooks in formal mode with replay/rate/size controls; keep local Secret resolution and one-time material delivery behind narrow channels. Paused drafts and policy-gated work fail closed unless a human creates an authorized one-off contract.
units.responsibilityConflict: The responsible-human revision snapshot is directly aligned with Company OS and is a notable positive. However, many service tests call with an empty actor; an assigned Agent can restore when the snapshot still assigns itself; public signingMode none and webhook activity-gate bypass can initiate work without a matched human decision; and stored plain variables/env can change authority or expose data without a data contract. Initiation records also stop short of approvals, evidence and accountable terminal acceptance.

units.securityFindings: CRITICAL unauthenticated-trigger risk: signingMode none accepts any public request and webhooks explicitly bypass the external-activity gate. CRITICAL responsibility/authorization gap: no approval or immutable model/tool/permission/data/budget contract is bound to dispatch; many service calls use no actor. HIGH data/Secret gap: resolved variables and plain env values persist in run/revision/issue state, while sensitivity and Connector/export redaction are untested. HIGH webhook gap: timestamp replay/freshness negatives, repeated signatures, rate/size/content-type and constant-time behavior are absent. HIGH idempotency gap: concurrent coalescing is strong but client intent keys and cross-node/process retries are untested; idle sequential retries create fresh issues by design. HIGH autonomous-change risk: an assigned Agent may restore an executable revision when it remains the assignee. POSITIVE: responsible human is snapshotted into automatic runs, restore is append-only, stale writes conflict, unsafe reporting chains fail, trigger snapshots exclude Secret values/IDs, Secret public identity rotates on restore, concurrent dispatch serializes and wakeup failure cleans orphan issues.
